'''Bojan Bogdanović''' ({{IPA|hr|bǒjan boɡdǎːnovitɕ}}; born 18 April 1989) is a Croatian former professional [[basketball]] player. Standing at {{height|ft=6|in=7}}, he played the [[small forward]] position. In the [[National Basketball Association]] (NBA), Bogdanović played for the [[Brooklyn Nets]], [[Washington Wizards]], [[Indiana Pacers]], [[Utah Jazz]], [[Detroit Pistons]], and [[New York Knicks]]. He also represented the [[Croatia men's national basketball team|Croatian national team]] internationally.

==Professional career==
===Early years===
Born in [[Mostar]], [[Bosnia and Herzegovina]], Bogdanović started his basketball career in 2004 with his hometown club [[HKK Zrinjski Mostar|Zrinjski Mostar]] where he played for one season. In 2005, he signed a five-year deal with [[Real Madrid Baloncesto|Real Madrid]], but was [[loan (sports)|loaned]] back to Zrinjski Mostar for the 2005–06 season. In 2006–07 and 2007–08, he played for Real Madrid's junior team, [[Real Madrid Baloncesto B|Real Madrid B]], in Spain's [[Spanish basketball league system|4th-tier league]], the [[Liga EBA]]. In 2008, he was loaned to [[CB Murcia]] for the 2008–09 season. In January 2009, he re-joined Real Madrid's junior team, Real Madrid B. Following the 2008–09 season, he parted ways with Real Madrid.<ref name=madrid>[http://www.sportando.com/en/cups/euroleague/78701/cibona-bags-young-forward-bojan-bogdanovic.html Cibona bags young forward Bojan Bogdanovic], sportando.com; accessed 20 July 2016.</ref>

=== Cibona Zagreb (2009–2011) ===
[[File:Bojan_Bogdanovi%C4%87_2010.jpg|thumb|left|Bogdanović with Cibona|100px]]
In August 2009, Bogdanović signed a four-year deal with [[KK Cibona|Cibona Zagreb]].<ref name="madrid"/> In July 2010, he signed a three-year contract extension with Cibona. Bogdanovic cites this relation as part of the reason he has decided to represent Croatia internationally.<ref>[http://www.sportando.com/en/cups/adriatic-league/83396/cibona-adds-two-extends-two.html Cibona adds two, extends two] {{Webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20141016213755/http://www.sportando.com/en/cups/adriatic-league/83396/cibona-adds-two-extends-two.html |date=16 October 2014 }}, sportando.com; accessed 20 July 2016.</ref> Following the 2010–11 season, he parted ways with Cibona.<ref>[http://www.sportando.com/en/europe/turkey/86048/bojan-bogdanovic-to-sign-with-fenerbahce.html Bojan Bogdanovic to sign with Fenerbahce?] {{Webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20141016213539/http://www.sportando.com/en/europe/turkey/86048/bojan-bogdanovic-to-sign-with-fenerbahce.html |date=16 October 2014 }}, sportando.com; accessed 20 July 2016.</ref>

=== Fenerbahçe Beko (2011–2014) ===
On 19 June 2011, Bogdanović signed a multi-year deal with [[Fenerbahçe S.K. (basketball)|Fenerbahçe Beko]].<ref>[http://www.sportando.com/en/europe/turkey/86579/fenerbahce-announces-bogdanovic-and-gist.html Fenerbahce announces Bogdanovic and Gist] {{Webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20141016213757/http://www.sportando.com/en/europe/turkey/86579/fenerbahce-announces-bogdanovic-and-gist.html |date=16 October 2014 }}, sportando.com; accessed 20 July 2016.</ref> On 23 June 2011, he was selected with the 31st overall pick in the [[2011 NBA draft]] by the [[Miami Heat]]. He was later traded to the [[Minnesota Timberwolves]], and then again to the [[New Jersey Nets]] on draft night.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/timberwolves/news/pressrelease_Wolves_Complete_Five_Draft_Night_Trades_2011_06_24.html|title=Wolves Complete Five Draft-Night Trades|work=NBA.com|date=24 June 2011|access-date=6 July 2014}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/nets/news/Bogdanovic_Rights_Release_110624.html|title=NETS Acquire Draft Rights to Bojan Bogdanovic|work=NBA.com|date=24 June 2011|access-date=6 July 2014}}</ref>

In September 2012, Fenerbahçe confirmed Bogdanović would return for the 2012–13 season.<ref>[http://www.sportando.com/en/europe/turkey/95198/pianigiani-dincer-bojan-bogdanovic-will-stay-with-us.html Pianigiani, Dincer: 'Bojan Bogdanovic will stay with us'], sportando.com; accessed 20 July 2016.</ref> In July 2013, following a breakdown in negotiations with the [[Brooklyn Nets]] on a possible contract buy-out, Bogdanović announced his decision to return to Fenerbahçe for the 2013–14 season.<ref>[http://www.sportando.com/en/europe/turkey/103496/zeljko-obradovic-bojan-bogdanovic-told-me-that-he-ll-stay.html Zeljko Obradovic: 'Bojan Bogdanovic told me that he'll stay'], sportando.com; accessed 20 July 2016.</ref>

=== Brooklyn Nets (2014–2017) ===
On July 20, 2014, Bogdanović signed a three-year, $10 million contract with the [[Brooklyn Nets]].<ref>[http://www.nba.com/nets/news/brooklyn-nets-sign-bojan-bogdanovic Brooklyn Nets Sign Bojan Bogdanovic] {{webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140723172453/http://www.nba.com/nets/news/brooklyn-nets-sign-bojan-bogdanovic |date=23 July 2014 }}, nba.com; accessed 20 July 2016.</ref><ref>[https://www.sbnation.com/nba/2014/7/7/5878609/nets-sign-bojan-bogdanovic Nets agree to sign Bojan Bogdanovic to 3-year deal], sbnation.com; accessed 20 July 2016.</ref> After starting the first 19 games of the 2014–15 season alongside [[Joe Johnson (basketball)|Joe Johnson]] on the wing, Bogdanović lost his starting spot on December 10 against the [[Chicago Bulls]] in favour of [[Sergey Karasev]].<ref>[http://www.netsdaily.com/2015/1/3/7485929/bojan-bogdanovic-continues-to-ride-the-pine Bojan Bogdanovic continues to ride the pine]</ref> He later regained his starting spot on January 10 against the [[Detroit Pistons]].<ref>[http://www.nba.com/games/20150110/BKNDET/gameinfo.html Jennings' 20 in 2nd half helps Pistons down Nets, 98-93] {{Webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190209131622/http://www.nba.com/games/20150110/BKNDET/gameinfo.html |date=9 February 2019 }}, nba.com; accessed 20 July 2016.</ref> In the Nets' regular season finale on April 15 against the [[Orlando Magic]], Bogdanović had a season-best game with 28 points on 12-of-17 shooting to help the Nets clinch the No. 8 seed in the Eastern Conference with a 101–88 win.<ref>[http://www.nba.com/games/20150415/ORLBKN/gameinfo.html Nets clinch playoff spot after win, Pacers loss] {{Webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170921194615/http://www.nba.com/games/20150415/ORLBKN/gameinfo.html |date=21 September 2017 }}, nba.com; accessed 20 July 2016.</ref> The Nets lost to the [[Atlanta Hawks]] 4–2 in the first round of the playoffs.

On November 11, 2015, Bogdanović helped the Nets record their first win of the season, scoring a season-high 22 points in a 106–98 victory over the [[Houston Rockets]].<ref>[http://www.nba.com/games/20151111/BKNHOU/gameinfo.html Bogdanovic leads Nets to 1st win, 106-98 over Houston], nba.com; accessed 20 July 2016.</ref> He topped that season high mark with 24 points on February 26, in a 116–106 win over the [[Phoenix Suns]].<ref>[http://www.nba.com/games/20160225/BKNPHX/gameinfo.html Bogdanovic, Nets top Suns in battle of lowly teams] {{Webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160226173635/http://www.nba.com/games/20160225/BKNPHX/gameinfo.html |date=26 February 2016 }}, nba.com; accessed 20 July 2016.</ref> On March 5, 2016, he scored a career-high 44 points in a 131–114 win over the [[Philadelphia 76ers]]. His total was the most for a Nets player since [[Deron Williams]] scored 57 on March 4, 2012, and the most by any Nets player since the team moved to Brooklyn prior to the 2012–13 season.<ref>[http://www.nba.com/games/20160315/PHIBKN/gameinfo.html Bogdanovic scores career-high 44, Nets beat 76ers 131-114] {{Webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170305003342/http://www.nba.com/games/20160315/PHIBKN/gameinfo.html |date=5 March 2017 }}, nba.com; accessed 20 July 2016.</ref> In the Nets' regular season finale on April 13, he tied his career high with seven three-pointers and scored 29 points in a 103–96 loss to the [[Toronto Raptors]].<ref>[http://www.nba.com/games/20160413/TORBKN/gameinfo.html Raptors rest starters, beat Nets 103-96 in playoff tuneup] {{Webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160413114547/http://www.nba.com/games/20160413/TORBKN/gameinfo.html |date=13 April 2016 }}, nba.com; accessed 20 July 2016.</ref> The Nets lost their final 10 games of the season and finished with a 21–61 win–loss record.

In the Nets' season opener on October 26, 2016, Bogdanović scored a team-high 21 points in a 122–117 loss to the [[Boston Celtics]].<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.espn.com.au/nba/recap?gameId=400899380|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20161027193148/http://www.espn.com.au/nba/recap?gameId=400899380|url-status=dead|archive-date=27 October 2016|title=Thomas scores 25, Celtics fight off Nets 122-117|work=ESPN.com|date=26 October 2016|access-date=27 October 2016}}</ref>

===Washington Wizards (2017)===
[[File:Mario Hezonja, Bojan Bogdanovic (33236676916).jpg|thumb|right|Bogdanović (background) with the Wizards in March 2017]]
On February 22, 2017, Bogdanović was traded, along with [[Chris McCullough]], to the [[Washington Wizards]] in exchange for [[Andrew Nicholson (basketball)|Andrew Nicholson]], [[Marcus Thornton (basketball, born 1987)|Marcus Thornton]] and a 2017 protected first-round draft pick.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://wizardstoday.monumentalsportsnetwork.com/2017/02/22/wizards-acquire-bojan-bogdanovic-and-chris-mccullough|title=Wizards Acquire Bojan Bogdanovic and Chris McCullough|work=monumentalsportsnetwork.com|date=22 February 2017|access-date=22 February 2017|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170330023448/https://wizardstoday.monumentalsportsnetwork.com/2017/02/22/wizards-acquire-bojan-bogdanovic-and-chris-mccullough|archive-date=30 March 2017|url-status=dead}}</ref> On March 1, he had a 27-point effort in a 105–96 win over the [[Toronto Raptors]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/recap?gameId=400899393|title=Wizards snap 8-game skid against Raptors with 105-96 win|work=ESPN.com|date=1 March 2017|access-date=2 March 2017}}</ref> Four days later, he scored 15 of his 27 points and made five of his career-high eight three-pointers, including the game-winner, during the fourth quarter of the Wizards' 115–114 win over the [[Orlando Magic]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/recap?gameId=400900325|title=Bogdanovic hits 8 3-pointers, Wizards beat Magic 115-114|work=ESPN.com|date=5 March 2017|access-date=6 March 2017}}</ref> On March 7, he scored 29 points and set a franchise record for free throws made by going 16 of 16 in a 131–127 win over the [[Phoenix Suns]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/recap?gameId=400900343|title=Bogdanovic, Beal, Wall lead Wizards past pesky Suns, 131-127|work=ESPN.com|date=7 March 2017|access-date=7 March 2017}}</ref>

===Indiana Pacers (2017–2019)===
On July 10, 2017, Bogdanović signed a two-year, $21 million contract with the [[Indiana Pacers]].<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/pacers/news/pacers-sign-bojan-bogdanovic|title=Pacers Sign Bojan Bogdanovic|work=NBA.com|date=10 July 2017|access-date=10 July 2017}}</ref> In his Pacers' debut on October 18, 2017, Bogdanović scored 14 points in a 140–131 win over the [[Brooklyn Nets]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/recap?gameId=400974701|title=Revamped Pacers rely on new faces to cut down Nets 140-131|work=ESPN.com|date=18 October 2017|access-date=18 October 2017}}</ref> On February 5, 2018, he scored a season-high 29 points in a 111–102 loss to the [[Washington Wizards]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/recap?gameId=400975537|title=Wizards beat Pacers 111-102, win 5th straight without Wall|work=ESPN.com|date=5 February 2018|access-date=5 February 2018}}</ref> On March 5, he tied his season high with 29 points in a 92–89 win over the [[Milwaukee Bucks]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/recap?gameId=400975697|title=Bogdanovic leads Pacers over Bucks 92-89|work=ESPN.com|date=5 March 2018|access-date=5 March 2018}}</ref> In Game 3 of the Pacers' first-round playoff series against the [[Cleveland Cavaliers]], Bogdanović scored 19 of his then playoff career-high 30 points in the second half, finishing 7 of 9 on 3-pointers, in a 92–90 win that saw the Pacers take a 2–1 lead.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/recap?gameId=401029424|title=Pacers erase 17-point deficit to take 2-1 lead over Cavs|work=ESPN.com|date=20 April 2018|access-date=20 April 2018}}</ref> The Pacers went on to lose the series in seven games.

On December 1, Bogdanović scored a then season-high 27 points in a 111–110 loss to the [[Sacramento Kings]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/recap?gameId=401071017|title=Cauley-Stein's putback dunk lifts Kings past Pacers 111-110|work=ESPN.com|date=1 December 2018|access-date=2 December 2018}}</ref> On February 2, 2019, he set a new season high with 31 points in a 95–88 win over the [[Miami Heat]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/recap?gameId=401071453|title=Pacers top Heat 95-88, end 4-game winless streak|work=ESPN.com|date=2 February 2019|access-date=10 February 2019}}</ref> On February 7, he scored 29 points in a 116–92 win over the [[Los Angeles Clippers]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/recap?gameId=401071484|title=Bogdanovic scores 29, Pacers beat short-handed Clippers|work=ESPN.com|date=7 February 2019|access-date=28 February 2019}}</ref> On February 11, he was named Eastern Conference Player of the Week for Week 17 of the 2018–19 season, thus marking his first career player of the week award.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.nba.com/pacers/news/bojan-bogdanovic-named-eastern-conference-player-week|title=Bojan Bogdanovic Named Eastern Conference Player of the Week|work=NBA.com|date=11 February 2019|access-date=12 February 2019}}</ref> On February 28, he set a new season high with 37 points in a 122–115 win over the [[Minnesota Timberwolves]].<ref>{{cite web|last=Rappaport|first=Greg|url=https://www.nba.com/pacers/rewind-pacers-timberwolves-190228|title=Game Rewind: Pacers 122, Timberwolves 115|work=NBA.com|date=28 February 2019|access-date=28 February 2019}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/recap?gameId=401071595|title=Bogdanovic has season-high 35 points, Pacers top Wolves|work=ESPN.com|date=28 February 2019|access-date=28 February 2019}}</ref> On March 24, he scored 26 of his 35 points in the first half of the Pacers' 124–88 win over the [[Denver Nuggets]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/recap?gameId=401071770|title=Bogdanovic scores 35, Pacers blow out Nuggets 124-88|work=ESPN.com|date=24 March 2019|access-date=25 March 2019}}</ref>

===Utah Jazz (2019–2022)===
On July 7, 2019, Bogdanović signed a four-year, $73 million contract with the [[Utah Jazz]],<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.nba.com/jazz/news/jazz-sign-forward-bojan-bogdanovic|title=Jazz Sign Forward Bojan Bogdanović|work=NBA.com|date=7 July 2019}}</ref> making him the all-time highest-paid Croatian athlete.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://sportske.jutarnji.hr/kosarka/nba/sve-je-to-divno-i-krasno-ali-te-price-me-umaraju-najplaceniji-hrvat-u-povijesti-koji-zaraduje-oko-120-milijuna-kuna-godisnje-progovorio-o-placi/9104306/|title='SVE JE TO DIVNO I KRASNO, ALI TE PRIČE ME UMARAJU!' Najplaćeniji Hrvat u povijesti, koji zarađuje oko 120 milijuna kuna godišnje, progovorio o plaći|date=11 July 2019|work=[[Sportske novosti]]|language=hr|access-date=12 July 2019}}</ref> He hit two buzzer-beating game-winners in his first season with Utah: November 8, 2019, against the [[Milwaukee Bucks]] and February 9, 2020, at the [[Houston Rockets]]. On May 19, the Jazz announced that Bogdanović had undergone a successful surgery in repairing a ruptured ligament in his right wrist<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.nba.com/jazz/news/bojan-bogdanovic-undergoes-surgery-repair-ruptured-ligament-wrist|title=Bojan Bogdanovic undergoes surgery to repair ruptured ligament in wrist|date=19 May 2020|website=NBA.com|access-date=19 May 2020}}</ref> and was expected to be sidelined for the remainder of the [[2019–20 NBA season|2019–20 season]].

On May 1, 2021, Bogdanović scored a season-high 34 points on 12-of-22 shooting from the field and 6-of-11 from the three, in addition to four rebounds and four assists across 39 minutes in a 106–102 win against the [[Toronto Raptors]].<ref>{{Cite web|title=Jazz's Bojan Bogdanovic: Stars in win over Raptors|url=https://www.cbssports.com/fantasy/basketball/news/jazzs-bojan-bogdanovic-stars-in-win-over-raptors/|access-date=2021-05-02|work=CBS Sports|date=2 May 2021}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|title=Bogdanovic scores 34 as Jazz rally to beat Raptors 106-102|url=https://www.foxsports.com/stories/nba/bogdanovic-scores-34-as-jazz-rally-to-beat-raptors-106102|access-date=2021-05-02|work=FOX Sports}}</ref> On May 7, Bogdanović scored a career-high 48 points on 16-of-23 shooting from the field and 8-of-11 from the arc in a 127–120 win over the [[Denver Nuggets]].<ref>{{Cite web|title=Bogdanovic scores career-high 48 points, Jazz beat Nuggets|url=https://www.cbssports.com/nba/news/bogdanovic-scores-career-high-48-points-jazz-beat-nuggets/|access-date=2021-05-08|website=CBSSports.com|date=8 May 2021}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|title=Bojan Bogdanovic's career-high 48 points carry Utah Jazz over Nuggets in playoff-like atmosphere|url=https://sltrib.com/sports/jazz/2021/05/07/bojan-bogdanovics-career|access-date=2021-05-08|work=The Salt Lake Tribune}}</ref>

On May 23, during the first round of the playoffs, Bogdanović recorded 29 points, five assists and two steals in a 109–112 Game 1 loss to the [[Memphis Grizzlies]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=8TH-SEEDED MEMPHIS BEATS NO. 1-SEEDED JAZZ IN SERIES OPENER |url=https://www.nba.com/game/0042000141 |access-date=January 29, 2023 |website=NBA.com}}</ref> The Jazz ended up winning the series in five games. On June 16, during the second round of the playoffs, Bogdanović scored 32 points, alongside nine 3-pointers, in a 111–119 Game 5 loss to the [[Los Angeles Clippers]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=CLIPPERS BEAT JAZZ 119-111 TO TAKE SERIES LEAD |url=https://www.nba.com/game/0042000225 |access-date=January 29, 2023 |website=NBA.com}}</ref> The Jazz lost the series in six games.

On January 5, 2022, Bogdanović recorded a season-high 36 points, alongside 13 rebounds and four assists, in a 115–109 win over the [[Denver Nuggets]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=ROADIES: BOGDANOVIC SCORES 36, JAZZ BEAT NUGGETS 115-109 |url=https://www.nba.com/game/0022100575 |access-date=January 29, 2023 |website=NBA.com}}</ref>

On April 16, during the first round of the playoffs, Bogdanović logged 26 points and four assists in a 99–93 Game 1 win over the [[Dallas Mavericks]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=Utah Jazz hold on in the clutch, steal Game 1 in Dallas |url=https://www.sltrib.com/sports/jazz/2022/04/16/utah-jazz-hold-clutch/ |access-date=April 16, 2022 |work=The Salt Lake Tribune}}</ref> Two days later, he scored 25 points in a 104–110 Game 2 loss.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Brunson scores 41, Mavs make 22 3s in Game 2 win vs Jazz |url=https://www.espn.com/nba/recap/_/gameId/401430232 |access-date=April 19, 2022 |website=ESPN.com}}</ref> The Jazz lost the series in six games.

===Detroit Pistons (2022–2024)===
On September 26, 2022, Bogdanović was traded to the [[Detroit Pistons]] in exchange for [[Kelly Olynyk]], [[Saben Lee]], and minimal cash considerations.<ref>{{cite web|first=Angie|last=Treasure|title=Utah Jazz Acquire Kelly Olynyk, Saben Lee and Cash Considerations|url=https://www.nba.com/jazz/news/utah-jazz-acquire-kelly-olynyk-saben-lee-and-cash-considerations|website=NBA.com|publisher=Utah Jazz|date=September 26, 2022|access-date=September 27, 2022}}</ref> Bogdanović made his Pistons debut on October 19, logging 24 points and five rebounds in a 113–109 win over the [[Orlando Magic]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=BOGDANOVIC SHINES IN DETROIT DEBUT, HELPS PISTONS BEAT MAGIC |url=https://www.nba.com/game/0022200003 |access-date=January 29, 2023 |website=NBA.com}}</ref> On October 31, he signed a two-year, $39.1 million contract extension with the Pistons.<ref>{{Cite web |title=DETROIT PISTONS SIGN BOJAN BOGDANOVIĆ TO A CONTRACT EXTENSION |url=https://www.nba.com/pistons/news/detroit-pistons-sign-bojan-bogdanovic-to-a-contract-extension |access-date=January 29, 2023 |website=NBA}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |title=Bojan Bogdanovic, Pistons reach 2-year, $39.1 million extension |url=https://www.espn.com/nba/story/_/id/34912353/bojan-bogdanovic-pistons-reach-2-year-391-million-extension |access-date=January 29, 2023 |website=ESPN|date=30 October 2022 }}</ref> On December 11, 2022, Bogdanović scored a season-high 35 points in a 124–117 loss to the [[Los Angeles Lakers]].<ref>{{cite web |title=Los Angeles Lakers at Detroit Pistons Box Score, December 11, 2022 |url=https://www.basketball-reference.com/boxscores/202212110DET.html |website=Basketball Reference |access-date=February 9, 2024}}</ref>

On January 3, 2024, Bogdanović scored a season-high 36 points and accumulated 7 rebounds in a return to [[Utah Jazz|Utah]], a 154–148 overtime loss.<ref>{{cite web |title=JAZZ SNAG WIN IN OT |url=https://www.nba.com/game/det-vs-uta-0022300474/box-score |website=NBA.com |publisher=NBA |access-date=February 9, 2024}}</ref>

===New York Knicks (2024)===
On 8 February 2024, Bogdanović and [[Alec Burks]] were traded to the [[New York Knicks]] in exchange for [[Ryan Arcidiacono]], [[Malachi Flynn]], [[Evan Fournier]], [[Quentin Grimes]] and two second-round picks.<ref>{{cite web|title=New York Knicks Acquire Bojan Bogdanovic and Alec Burks|url=https://www.nba.com/knicks/news/new-york-knicks-acquire-bojan-bogdanovic-and-alec-burks|website=NBA.com|date=8 February 2024|access-date=8 February 2024}}</ref> On 30 April 2024, it was announced that Bogdanović would miss the remainder of the [[2024 NBA playoffs]] after undergoing season-ending surgeries on his left foot and left wrist.<ref>{{cite web|title=Bojan Bogdanovic will be out for the remainder of the 2024 NBA Postseason|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/team/injuries/_/name/ny/new-york-knicks|website=ESPN.com|date=20 April 2024|access-date=11 May 2024}}</ref> On 6 July 2024, Bogdanović was traded back to the [[Brooklyn Nets]] alongside [[Mamadi Diakite]], [[Shake Milton]] who was signed and traded, four unprotected first-round picks, an unprotected pick swap and a second-round pick in exchange for [[Mikal Bridges]], [[Keita Bates-Diop]] and a second–round pick.<ref>{{cite web|title=Brooklyn Nets Complete Trade With New York Knicks|url=https://www.nba.com/nets/news/brooklyn-nets-complete-trade-with-new-york-knicks|website=NBA.com|date=6 July 2024|access-date=6 July 2024}}</ref> The trade was notable for being the first trade between the two rival franchises since 1983.

Bogdanović's injuries prevented him from playing for the Nets. On 19 February 2025, it was announced that Bogdanovic would undergo a season ending foot surgery.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Charania |first=Shams  |author-link=Shams Charania |date=19 February 2025 |title=Sources: Nets' Bojan Bogdanovic to have season-ending foot surgery |url=https://www.espn.com/nba/story/_/id/43919202/sources-nets-bojan-bogdanovic-season-ending-foot-surgery |access-date=February 19, 2025 |website=espn.com}}</ref> He was waived later that day to free up roster space for [[Killian Hayes]].<ref>{{Cite web |date=2025-02-19 |title=Report: Nets waiving veteran F Bojan Bogdanovic |url=https://www.yardbarker.com/nba/articles/report_nets_waiving_veteran_f_bojan_bogdanovic/s1_17045_41781720 |access-date=2025-02-19 |work=Yardbarker}}</ref> On 29 June 2025, Bogdanović announced his retirement, citing his recurring foot injuries.<ref>{{cite web |title=Bojan Bogdanovic retires after 10 NBA seasons |url=https://www.espn.com/nba/story/_/id/45609272/bojan-bogdanovic-retires-10-nba-seasons |website=ESPN.com |date=29 June 2025 |access-date=29 June 2025}}</ref>

==National team career==
[[File:Bojan Bogdanovic, Austria v Croatia 2012 (cropped).jpg|thumb|200px|Bogdanović playing with the [[Croatia national basketball team|Croatia national team]] in 2012]]

Bogdanović played for the Croatian Under-16 national team in 2005, the Under-18 team in 2006 and 2007, and the Under-20 team in 2009. In 2010, he joined the senior [[Croatia national basketball team|Croatian national team]] for the [[2010 FIBA World Championship]]. In July 2012, the Croatian national team's [[head coach]], [[Jasmin Repeša]], kicked Bogdanović off the team for disciplinary reasons.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://archive.sportando.basketball/it/cat/nba/94011/bojan-bogdanovic-kicked-out-of-croatian-national-team.html|title=Bojan Bogdanovic kicked out of Croatian National Team|date=29 July 2012|work=Sportando.com|access-date=5 June 2019}}</ref>

He re-joined Croatia for the [[FIBA EuroBasket 2013|2013 EuroBasket]] and the [[2014 FIBA Basketball World Cup|2014 FIBA World Cup]]. He also represented Croatia at the [[2015 EuroBasket]],<ref>{{cite news|title=CROATIA UNVEIL AMBITIOUS EUROBASKET SQUAD|url=http://www.eurobasket2015.org/en/compID_qMRZdYCZI6EoANOrUf9le2.season_2015.roundID_9322.coid_W0rFwutQJaUwHCCv5u3xf0.articleMode_on.html|access-date=13 September 2015|work=eurobasket2015.org|date=4 September 2015|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150913045910/http://www.eurobasket2015.org/en/compID_qMRZdYCZI6EoANOrUf9le2.season_2015.roundID_9322.coid_W0rFwutQJaUwHCCv5u3xf0.articleMode_on.html|archive-date=13 September 2015|url-status=usurped}}</ref> where they were eliminated in the eighth finals by [[Czech Republic national basketball team|Czech Republic]].<ref>{{cite news|title=CZECHS MAKE FIRST QUARTER-FINAL TRIP|url=http://www.eurobasket2015.org/en/compID_qMRZdYCZI6EoANOrUf9le2.season_2015.roundID_9322.coid_jqFXDJwUH0AvptWBlLCC63.articleMode_on.html|access-date=13 September 2015|work=.eurobasket2015.org|date=13 September 2015|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150914214822/http://www.eurobasket2015.org/en/compID_qMRZdYCZI6EoANOrUf9le2.season_2015.roundID_9322.coid_jqFXDJwUH0AvptWBlLCC63.articleMode_on.html|archive-date=14 September 2015|url-status=usurped}}</ref> Over six tournament games, he averaged 10.8 points, 3.4 rebounds and 1.2 assists on 31.5% shooting from the field.<ref>{{cite web|title=Bojan Bogdanovic|url=http://www.eurobasket2015.org/en/compID_qMRZdYCZI6EoANOrUf9le2.season_2015.roundID_9322.teamID_2168.playerID_47907.html|website=eurobasket2015.org|publisher=FIBA Europe|access-date=13 September 2015|archive-date=27 November 2015|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20151127204359/http://www.eurobasket2015.org/en/compID_qMRZdYCZI6EoANOrUf9le2.season_2015.roundID_9322.teamID_2168.playerID_47907.html|url-status=usurped}}</ref>

Bogdanović also represented Croatia at [[Basketball at the 2016 Summer Olympics – Men's tournament|2016 Summer Olympics in Rio de Janeiro]]. He led all scorers with 25.3 points per game, while shooting 50.6 percent from the field and 45 percent from the 3-point line.<ref>{{cite web|title=Bojan Bogdanovic|url=https://www.fiba.basketball/olympics/2016/playerstats|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160808153356/http://www.fiba.com/olympics/2016/playerstats|url-status=live|archive-date=8 August 2016}}</ref>
